learningObjectives: Identify interaction patterns that communicate system behavior.
Design appropriate feedback for user actions and system states.
Understand the role of triggers, responses, and state changes in microinteractions.
Use microinteractions to improve clarity without adding unnecessary complexity.

activities.title: Interaction State Explorer
activities.instruction: Explore each interaction state and identify what it communicates.

content.concept: Interaction states communicate what users can do, what they are currently doing, and what the system is doing.
content.tip: Explore the states in sequence and observe how the interface communicates system status.

descriptions: Provides visual feedback when the pointer is over an element.
Confirms that an action is being activated.
Shows that an action is unavailable.
Communicates that processing is taking place.
Confirms that an operation completed successfully.
Communicates that an operation failed or requires correction.

activities.title: Feedback Matcher
activities.instruction: Match each user action with suitable system feedback.

content.concept: Feedback confirms actions and communicates results through visual, textual, motion, or other appropriate cues.
content.tip: Choose feedback that clearly communicates the result without distracting from the task.

activities.title: Microinteraction Builder
activities.instruction: Build a microinteraction from trigger to response.

content.concept: A microinteraction connects a trigger, system response, feedback, and resulting state change.
content.tip: Build the interaction in the order the user and system experience it.

activities.title: Feedback Timing Lab
activities.instruction: Adjust feedback timing and observe how it affects the experience.

content.concept: Feedback should appear at an appropriate time so users understand whether an action succeeded, failed, or is still processing.
content.tip: Compare immediate, delayed, and excessive feedback to identify the timing that best supports the task.
